title: Fowler House
summary: The Fowler House in Freetown belonged to Montaukett gardener George Lewis Fowler and Sarah Melissa Horton Fowler. Current architectural research indicates that the house was built in Freetown around 1885, after Montaukett families faced dispossession at Indian Field, rather than moved intact from Montauk.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Montaukett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Physically relocated from the ancestral Montauk settlement of Indian Fields to the Freetown neighborhood, the Fowler House stands as a stark architectural record of developer Arthur Benson's campaign to remove the Montaukett people. Preserving this structure transforms an instrument of forced displacement into a powerful, enduring monument to the resilience and ongoing presence of indigenous families.
history_content: George Fowler was a Montaukett gardener whose family lived in Freetown after Arthur Benson's acquisition of Montaukett land at Indian Field. Research completed during preservation work indicates that the Fowler House was probably built at its present Freetown location around 1885. A neighboring house associated with Fowler's sister may have been moved from Indian Field, which likely contributed to the earlier confusion.
preservation_content: East Hampton Town designated the property a historic landmark in 2016 and completed major restoration work in 2018. Preservation Long Island and local researchers have used the house to expand public understanding of Montaukett family life, labor, dispossession, and Freetown history.
